title: Loss functions: MSE, cross-entropy, and the one that fits the task

videos.script: A network learns whatever its loss rewards. Change the loss, and you change what it learns. {{guess}} Six deliveries take between twelve and sixteen minutes. One takes an hour, in a storm. {{mean}} Ask squared error for the best single guess, and it says twenty and a half minutes. Nobody waited that long. Absolute error says fourteen, which is the typical delivery. {{pull}} The difference is the pull of one large error, squared. {{xent}} A classifier uses another loss: minus the log of the probability it gave the right answer. Confident and right costs almost nothing. Confident and wrong costs over a hundred times as much. {{nan}} Typed straight from the formula, it breaks on large scores and prints not a number. One subtraction fixes it. {{race}} Then a race on the digits. Same network, same seed, and only the loss changes. After one epoch, cross-entropy is ahead by almost forty points. {{metric}} Last, the loss you train on is not the number you judge by. Two models with the same accuracy can have very different losses. {{end}}
